<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dee7692f0bf5637c5c35609b9a27d42fe506b85d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `45c7b879023163af0fc3446555bcc5b96f1a1b22` — the merge of head `dd583360b3cad69acfdeee2be64d1ac0a6575e9a` into base `dee7692f0bf5637c5c35609b9a27d42fe506b85d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 45c7b879023163af0fc3446555bcc5b96f1a1b22 && git checkout 45c7b879023163af0fc3446555bcc5b96f1a1b22
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dee7692f0bf5637c5c35609b9a27d42fe506b85d dd583360b3cad69acfdeee2be64d1ac0a6575e9a && git checkout -B drift-repro dee7692f0bf5637c5c35609b9a27d42fe506b85d && git merge --no-ff dd583360b3cad69acfdeee2be64d1ac0a6575e9a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dee7692f0bf5637c5c35609b9a27d42fe506b85d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dee7692f0bf5637c5c35609b9a27d42fe506b85d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dd583360b3cad69acfdeee2be64d1ac0a6575e9a`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

**Readings** (2026-10-09T14:20Z): head `dd583360b` = `527974a2c` merged onto `origin/main` `dee7692f0`, which is also the merge-base, so the net diff is exactly the PR's 6 files (+463 / −24). Check-runs on the head: 34, latest per name 31 `success`, 3 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke — paths-filtered / opt-in), 0 failure; all seven required contexts `success`; the only annotation on the gate-carrying runs is the runner-image notice. Inputs: card #22463 body + 3 comments (triage `6079484598`, claim `6080361919`, dev report `6081229608`), PR body, file list, net diff, docs-drift comment `6081191779`.

**Published surface** — `@objectstack/plugin-auth` publishes `exports["."]` → `dist/index.d.ts` (`src/index.ts` carries `export * from './register-sso-provider.js'`) and `./rate-limit-storage` (untouched). Every change the diff makes to it:

- **W1** `runRequestDomainVerification(handle, request, options = {})` gains an optional third parameter — additive widening on a published export. RIGHT.
- **W2** `runVerifyDomain(handle, request, options = {})` — the same widening. RIGHT.
- Return types: the alias `DomainVerificationBridgeResult` replaces the inline intersection and is declared as exactly that intersection (`RegisterSsoFormResult & { body: … & { data?: any } }`) — neither widening nor narrowing. RIGHT.
- `SsoDomainVerificationBridgeOptions` (interface) and `DomainVerificationBridgeResult` (type alias) carry no `export` in `register-sso-provider.ts` — module-local in source, confirmed; not nameable from the entry. They are reachable *structurally* through W1/W2 (tsc emits them as non-exported declarations beside the signatures), so a consumer can pass `{ domainVerificationEnabled: true }` but cannot import either name. The dev's "the widening is only the optional parameter" holds. `domainVerificationDisabled()` / `codelessVendorNotFound()` are module-local functions, not published.
- `AuthPlugin`: no signature change; `registerAuthRoutes` is private. Nothing published moves there.
- **No other widening and no narrowing** anywhere in the published type surface. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body: RIGHT — and the only published widening is W1+W2, as the body states.

**Accept-set / answers on the two mounted doors** (`POST /api/v1/auth/admin/sso/request-domain-verification`, `…/verify-domain`):

- **R1** flag on, platform admin, unknown `providerId`: `400 DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_DISABLED` → `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, message `SSO provider "ID" was not found.` A refusal before and after — not a narrowing of the accept set; a corrected code AND status (ADR-0112). RIGHT. `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` is `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap[404]` (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts:187`) and plugin-auth already emits it (`admin-ban-endpoints.ts:103`, `admin-user-endpoints.ts:699`, `auth-plugin.ts:2494`, `:2601`, `admin-set-user-manager.ts:435`): **no new code**, no ledger edit, no `packages/spec` file in the diff; `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:error-status-conformance`) is `success` on this head. Triage's other prohibition holds too: the branch is `resp.status === 404 && !parsed?.code` (the pre-existing structured-`code` read, ADR-0112 pass-through) plus the caller's flag — `parsed.message` is never read, pinned by the empty-body / reworded-body unit pin.
- **R2** flag on, coded vendor 404 (`NO_PENDING_VERIFICATION`): passes through untouched (real-stack pin; A4 ablation red). RIGHT.
- **R3** flag off (`isSsoDomainVerificationEnabled()` false: SSO not wired, or wired with the switch off): `400 DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_DISABLED` as before, now returned after the `providerId` and URL checks and before `handle()`. The returned literal is byte-identical to the base's two inline literals (same md5 over the extracted object literal at base and head). On every in-repo composition the vendor's answer in this state was a code-less 404 — `buildPluginList` mounts `domainVerification` from the same `pluginConfig.ssoDomainVerification ?? OS_SSO_DOMAIN_VERIFICATION ?? false` expression (`auth-manager.ts:3035`, `:3907`) and `sso()` itself from `pluginConfig.sso ?? OS_SSO_ENABLED ?? false` = `isSsoWired()` (`:7020`), and `applyConfigPatch` discards the built instance on a config change (`:4353`) — so skipping the call changes no answer. RIGHT. The dogfood row at `packages/qa/dogfood/test/admin-route-nonadmin-refusal.dogfood.test.ts:307/312` (SSO off → 400 DISABLED) still holds; `Dogfood Regression Gate` `success`.
- **R4** no flag — the exported helpers called with two arguments. In-repo the only callers are `auth-plugin.ts:3086` and `:3104`, both now passing the flag; the cloud auth proxy (outside this repository and outside this review's inputs) is the two-argument caller. Default `{}` → `codelessVendorNotFound` → `domainVerificationDisabled()`: the vendor is still called first, the 404 test is unchanged, every other branch is untouched, the literal is byte-identical. **The no-flag path is the old mapping byte for byte**: RIGHT (pinned on the real ON stack and in the unit file, both 404 body shapes). Corollary the changeset states: that caller gets the fix only once it passes the flag.
- **R5** anonymous caller: `gateAdmin(c)` at `auth-plugin.ts:3084` / `:3102` returns before the bridge is called; the flag is read in the bridge's argument list, evaluated after the gate. 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`, on and off, vendor never asked — pinned ×4, A6 ablation red. RIGHT.
- **R6** missing `providerId` / bad URL with the flag off: `400 INVALID_REQUEST` first — the early return sits after both checks. RIGHT (unit pin).
- No in-repo consumer branches on `DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_DISABLED` (outside plugin-auth: the docs page, the ledger, the dogfood note only); the `sys_sso_provider` actions (`platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts:178`, `:208`) post to these doors and render the envelope.

**Test files**: `admin-sso-bridge-gate.test.ts` stand-in gains an `isSsoDomainVerificationEnabled` stub answering `true`, matching its `sso({ domainVerification: { enabled: true } })` vendor — RIGHT and necessary (the mounts now call the seam; a stand-in without it would answer 500).

**File list vs claim surface** (`6080361919`): `.changeset/22463-sso-domain-verification-unknown-provider.md`; `register-sso-provider.ts`; `auth-plugin.ts` with hunks at `:3073–3110` only (the two mounts, as the claim scoped it); three `plugin-auth` test files (one new). **Nothing outside the surface**: no `packages/spec`, no `content/docs`, no other package, no governed surface. Head repo = base repo; PR is draft; auto-merge not armed.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22463-sso-domain-verification-unknown-provider.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-auth': minor`, carrying `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. **Level RIGHT**: W1/W2 are additive widenings on published exports, which take at least `minor`; no narrowing anywhere (R1 moves one refusal to another refusal, R3/R4 keep the answer), so not breaking and no ADR-0087 marker is owed. `skip-changeset` would be wrong — plugin-auth is a released package (17.7.0) and the diff publishes. `Check Changeset` `success`.

Prose, sentence by sentence against the head:
- Title sentence (on, unknown `providerId` → `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, no longer `400 DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_DISABLED`) — `codelessVendorNotFound` with `=== true` behind both mounts; real-stack pin. TRUE.
- *Before* — the removed `resp.status === 404 && !parsed?.code` → DISABLED in both bridges; the vendor's two code-less 404s are pinned live in the precondition test. TRUE.
- *Now* — mounts hand `AuthManager.isSsoDomainVerificationEnabled()` (`auth-plugin.ts:3089`, `:3107`); off → DISABLED with the vendor no longer called (early return before `handle()`); on → code-less 404 → `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` naming the id; the decision never reads the wording. All TRUE.
- *Unchanged* — gate first (R5); missing `providerId` → `INVALID_REQUEST` (R6); an existing provider gets the vendor's answer: the DNS record and `NO_PENDING_VERIFICATION` are pinned on the real stack, `DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED` and a 403 ride the untouched default branch (`status: resp.status`, `code: parsed?.code || 'DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED'`; unit 502 pins). TRUE — "unchanged" by the diff not touching that branch, which the PR body says plainly.
- *The exported bridges* — optional third argument `{ domainVerificationEnabled?: boolean }`; omitted keeps the earlier mapping byte for byte (R4); a self-mounting host passes the setting. TRUE.

No sentence overstates the code. `Clause-②:` line: PR body and changeset both read `yes (widening)`; the claim foresaw amending it only if no exported signature changed — two did, so the line stands as written.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (report `6081229608`), each answered:
1. Real-stack pins in a new file rather than `in-process-session-renewal.pin.test.ts` — inside the declared surface; the untouched file's wall time reported before/after. Accepted.
2. `admin-sso-bridge-gate.test.ts` stand-in gains the flag seam — inside the surface; judged RIGHT in ①. Accepted.
3. `origin/main` `dee7692f0` merged in as `dd583360b` — that commit is the merge-base, so nothing rides into the net diff. Accepted.
4. Commit trailer per the repo's model-free pair — conforms. Accepted.
5. Two helper types module-local — verified in ①. Accepted.
6. Worktree cleanup — not a matter for this record.

`open_questions`: empty — nothing to answer.

`out_of_scope_findings`, judged:
- **`authInstance` boundary** — `isSsoDomainVerificationEnabled()` reads `this.config.plugins` and the env; a pre-built `AuthManagerOptions.authInstance` (`auth-manager.ts:623`, consumed once at `:1442`, preserved by `applyConfigPatch` at `:4353`) is not described by that config. A host injecting one with domain verification on while config/env say off would now get DISABLED at these doors without a vendor call, where before the vendor answered. **In-repo reach: zero producers** — repo-wide grep finds the declaration and its one use only; `AuthPluginConfig` in spec declares no such key; `AuthPlugin` builds its manager from `...this.options` (`auth-plugin.ts:442`, `:574`). That host already got `sso: false` from `isSsoWired()` in the capability advert (`auth-manager.ts:6963`) before this PR, so the inconsistency predates the diff. The acceptance note is the right carrier (no in-repo reproduction to file). Accepted, not escalated.
- **Env-read timing** (this review's own, same family): `buildPluginList` reads `OS_SSO_ENABLED` / `OS_SSO_DOMAIN_VERIFICATION` at the lazy build; `isSsoDomainVerificationEnabled()` reads them per request. A post-boot env mutation would make the two disagree. Pre-existing for `isSsoWired()`'s advert (`auth-plugin.ts:693`, `auth-manager.ts:6963`); no non-test code in the repo writes either var after boot (grep). Noted, not escalated.
- **Test-harness trap** (`createMemoryEngine` import brings `afterEach(restoreAllMocks)` along): observation; this PR's own counter is a plain instance wrapper with positive-control legs (A2/A3 red). Accepted.

**docs-drift-check** (`6081191779`): the diff touches no `content/docs` file. Six of the seven hand-written pages name `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` generically (404, "the requested resource does not exist") — the diff conforms to them and changes nothing they state. `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx:281–287` states the OFF answers: "step 1 answers 400 `DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_DISABLED`, step 2 passes the inner 404 through with an explanatory message". This diff does not change the OFF answer on either door — but that step-2 clause was **already false at the base**: since #10859 both doors answer `400 DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_DISABLED` when off (the removed base lines of `runVerifyDomain` show it; the dogfood note at `admin-route-nonadmin-refusal.dogfood.test.ts:312` records the change). **Escalated** as a pre-existing docs-only finding outside this PR's surface (the claim forbids `content/docs`): the owning seat files a docs-only card to reword that callout; not a reason to touch this PR. The page says nothing about the ON + unknown-provider case, so the new answer contradicts nothing written. The two release-owned pages are read-only and name the code generically.

Cloud auth proxy: outside this repository and this review's inputs; judged on R4 — the two-argument call keeps the old mapping byte for byte.
